mainTopic: The egg laid on ראש השנה after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment, and רב יוסף's principle that a voted decree needs a new vote to be cancelled
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a quoted משנה from ראש השנה. The משנה explains how late witnesses once confused the לויים, so the court stopped accepting witnesses after מנחה time, and both days of ראש השנה came to be kept as one holy unit. Because of that, an egg laid on the first day would be forbidden on the second. רבה says that once רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored all-day testimony after the חורבן, the egg became permitted. אביי challenges him from רב and שמואל, and רבה answers that a תנא outweighs אמוראים. The גמרא then reconciles רב and שמואל: their ruling is for בבל, while the משנה's change applies in ארץ ישראל. רב יוסף disagrees and says the egg stays forbidden, because a rule made by a vote of the Sages needs a new vote to cancel it. He proves this from the פסוקים at הר סיני. Further support comes from the rule that כרם רבעי near ירושלים had to be brought there to fill its markets, and a story about רבי אליעזר's vineyard begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Levites' mistake and the new rule about witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues. Once the לויים sang the wrong song, the court ruled that witnesses for the new month would be accepted only until מנחה time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the לויים made a mistake in the song. So the court decreed that witnesses would be accepted only until the time of the afternoon offering.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a quoted משנה (ראש השנה ל׳ ע״ב). It tells why the court stopped accepting witnesses late in the day: the late witnesses had caused the לויים to sing the wrong song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, witnesses were accepted all day. One time they came late, and the לויים did not know whether to sing the weekday שיר or the ראש השנה שיר at the afternoon תמיד. To avoid this confusion, the court set a cutoff: no witnesses after מנחה time.

keyTerms.meaning: they went wrong / made a mistake
the Levites, who sang in the בית המקדש
the daily song sung with the offerings
the time of the afternoon תמיד offering

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a quote. These words are not a new statement of the גמרא; they continue a משנה that the גמרא is citing.

phrases.english: and the Levites erred in the song.
phrases.notes: They didn't know whether to sing the weekday song or the ראש השנה song at the afternoon offering.

phrases.english: They instituted that they would not accept
the witnesses except until minchah time.
phrases.notes: After that cutoff, the month would be counted as 30 days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה quoted on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the two days of ראש השנה form one holy unit, so an egg laid on one day is forbidden on the other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ראש השנה ל׳ ע״ב

steps.title: Late witnesses: both days are kept holy
steps.stepSummary: If witnesses came after מנחה time, people kept that day as holy and also the next day as holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if witnesses came from מנחה time onward, they treated that day as holy and the next day as holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its story. Late witnesses meant two days were kept holy, and this created a two-day ראש השנה even in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the key point of the proof. The second day was not kept out of doubt; it was set up by a decree, together with the first day. So both days are treated like one long holy day, and an egg laid on day one is like an egg laid on יום טוב itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for calling the two days of ראש השנה a קדושה אחת (one unit of holiness). Two days of יום טוב in the diaspora are different, because they come only from doubt.

phrases.english: And if witnesses came
from minchah time and onward,
they observe that day as holy,
and the next day as holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה begun in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The two days of ראש השנה are one holy unit, so the egg is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the משנה in ראש השנה ל׳ ע״ב

steps.title: רבה: after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's decree, the egg is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that from the time of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment onward, an egg laid on one day of ראש השנה is permitted on the other day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: From the decree of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and onward, an egg is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה limits the proof we just saw. He says the 'one holy unit' rule belonged only to the period before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי changed things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two days were tied together only because of the cutoff rule for witnesses. If that cutoff was later removed, the reason for treating both days as one unit is gone. Then the second day is kept only out of doubt, and the egg becomes permitted.

phrases.english: Rabba said: From the ordinance of
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai onward,
an egg is permitted.
phrases.notes: An egg laid on one day of ראש השנה may be eaten on the other day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof from the משנה to the time before the later enactment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment, an egg laid on one day of ראש השנה is permitted on the other.

steps.title: Source: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored all-day testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings the משנה showing that after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי decreed that testimony for the new month be accepted all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי decreed that they should accept testimony about the new month all day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה backs up his statement with a משנה. It shows that the cutoff for witnesses was removed after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש, there was no afternoon שיר to get wrong, so the cutoff was no longer needed. Once witnesses were again accepted all day, the court knew the exact day of ראש השנה. Two days were kept only by people who were far away and in doubt, and one of those days was surely a weekday, so the egg is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
testimony about seeing the new moon

steps.whatToRemember: The 'one holy unit' status of ראש השנה came from the cutoff decree. רבה holds that once רבן יוחנן בן זכאי removed the cutoff, that status went away too.

phrases.english: As we learned: After the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כׇּל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: that they would accept testimony of the new month all day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רבה's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that the egg is permitted after the enactment
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ראש השנה ל׳ ע״ב

steps.title: אביי: רב and שמואל say the egg is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: both רב and שמואל ruled that the egg is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But רב and שמואל both say that the egg is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's ruling. Two great אמוראים, רב and שמואל, said the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל lived long after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Even so, they forbade the egg. This seems to show that the old 'one unit' status still applies, which contradicts רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely / but doesn't (a challenge opener)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
But don't Rav and Shmuel
both say:
An egg is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, וְהָא רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the egg is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Authoritative later אמוראים forbade the egg, so the enactment did not cancel the one-unit status.

steps.title: רבה: a תנא outranks אמוראים
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that he is quoting רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, a תנא, and אביי cannot refute that with אמוראים like רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I tell you רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and you tell me רב and שמואל?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects אביי's challenge. He points out that his source is a תנא, which carries more weight than any אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה does not try to explain רב and שמואל. He simply says their opinion cannot stand against a source from the תנאים. In his view, the conclusion drawn from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment wins.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying רב and שמואל disagree with the facts of the enactment. He is saying that his inference from a תנא's enactment outweighs their ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: I tell you Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
and you tell me Rav and Shmuel?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Hierarchy of authority (a תנא over אמוראים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל's ruling disproves רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A source from the תנאים outweighs the opinion of אמוראים, so רבה's ruling stands.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב and שמואל can forbid the egg when the משנה says רבן יוחנן בן זכאי changed the old system.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב and שמואל, the משנה is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and challenges רב and שמואל using the same משנה that רבה quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that after the חורבן, testimony for the new month was accepted all day again. That seems to cancel the reason the two days were treated as one holiness. So how can רב and שמואל still forbid the egg?

phrases.english: But according to Rav and Shmuel, the Mishnah is difficult!
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment brought in step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא now asks how רב and שמואל deal with the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and שמואל's ruling that the egg is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows the enactment ended the 'one long day' situation, so the egg should be permitted.

steps.title: One ruling is for בבל, the other for ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל's ruling applies to Jews outside ארץ ישראל. The משנה's situation applies to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this ruling is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources are talking about different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל ("us"), two days are still kept by the old custom, so ראש השנה is treated as one long holiness and the egg is forbidden. In ארץ ישראל ("them"), after the enactment each day is its own holiness, so the egg is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is for us (Jews in בבל)
And that is for them (Jews in ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is for us, and that is for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לַן, וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל contradict the משנה everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב and שמואל speak about outside ארץ ישראל. The משנה's change applies in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the egg stays forbidden even after the enactment
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees with רבה and says that even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment, the egg is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Even from the time of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment and onward, an egg is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion appears. רב יוסף holds that the enactment did not make the egg permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the enactment removed the reason for the prohibition, so the egg became permitted. רב יוסף says it stays forbidden, even in ארץ ישראל. His reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Enactment, a rule the Sages set up

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 8. Step 8 forbade the egg only outside ארץ ישראל. רב יוסף forbids it even in ארץ ישראל, after the enactment.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ —
phrases.english: Even from the enactment of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and onward —
the egg is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אַף מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion opposed to רבה's statement in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment, an egg laid on one day of ראש השנה is forbidden on the other day.

steps.title: The reason: a rule made by a vote needs a new vote to cancel it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the egg prohibition was set by a vote of the Sages, and only a new vote can cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is a matter made by a vote, and any matter made by a vote needs another vote to permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רב יוסף's reason and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition was voted in by the Sages. Even if the reason behind it goes away, a voted rule does not cancel itself. A new vote is needed to permit it, and no such vote took place.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter decided by a vote of the Sages

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle in rabbinic law: a decree set by a formal vote stays in force even when its reason is gone, until a new vote cancels it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is a matter that was made by a vote,
and any matter made by a vote —
needs another vote to permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב יוסף's ruling in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רב יוסף forbid the egg after the enactment?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rule made by a vote needs a new vote to cancel it.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from הר סיני
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves his principle from פסוקים showing that restrictions from מתן תורה needed an explicit permission to be lifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From where do I say this? As it is written: "Go say to them: Return to your tents." And it says: "When the שופר sounds long, they may go up the mountain."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings פסוקים to support his rule that a prohibition needs an active permission to end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before מתן תורה, the people were told to stay away from their wives and not go up the mountain. Once the Torah was given, the reason was gone. Still, הקב"ה had to say out loud "return to your tents" and "they may go up the mountain." So a prohibition does not end by itself even when its purpose is over.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
To your tents (meaning: to your wives)
When the שופר (ram's horn) sounds long

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From where do I say it?
As it is written: "Go, say to them:
Return to your tents"
phrases.notes: Explicit permission to return to their wives.

phrases.english: And it says: "When the ram's horn sounds long,
they may go up the mountain."
phrases.notes: Explicit permission to go up the mountain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for the principle in step 10
steps.raayaObject: A prohibition needs an explicit permission to end, even when its reason is over.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים in דברים and שמות about the restrictions at הר סיני being explicitly lifted

steps.title: A ברייתא about כרם רבעי near ירושלים begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a ברייתא saying that fourth-year grapes from within a day's walk of ירושלים had to be brought there, and it lists the borders of that area.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: Fourth-year vineyard fruit would be brought up to ירושלים from a day's walk in every direction. And this is its border: עלת to the north, עקרבת to the south, לוד to the west, and the ירדן to the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as another support for רב יוסף. This part only sets up the case. The point that proves רב יוסף comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages required that כרם רבעי grown within a day's walk of ירושלים be brought there as fruit, not redeemed for money. This passage gives the rule and the four borders. The story that begins in step 14 and finishes on the next amud shows how this rule was later cancelled, which ties back to the idea of needing a new vote.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
Fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year, eaten in ירושלים like מעשר שני

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. Step 13 explains the reason for this rule, and step 14 begins the story that connects to רב יוסף's principle. That story finishes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And it was taught: a fourth-year vineyard
would be brought up to Jerusalem
from a one-day walk in every direction.
And this is its border:
Eilat to the north,
and Akrabat to the south,

phrases.aramaic: לוֹד מִן הַמַּעֲרָב, וְיַרְדֵּן מִן הַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: Lod to the west, and the Jordan to the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה עוֹלֶה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second support for רב יוסף's principle, starting with the background of the case
steps.raayaObject: That a rabbinic decree needs an active cancellation, even after its reason is gone
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about כרם רבעי near ירושלים (the related story begins in step 14 and continues on the next amud)

steps.title: The reason for bringing the fruit to ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: עולא (or some say רבה בר בר חנה), quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that the Sages required nearby fourth-year fruit to be brought to ירושלים so that its markets would be full of fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said (and some say it was רבה בר בר חנה) that רבי יוחנן said: What is the reason for this rule? To decorate the markets of ירושלים with fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain why the Sages made the rule from the ברייתא in Step 12. They wanted ירושלים to always have plenty of fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that fruit from within a day's walk must go to ירושלים is not a Torah requirement about distance. It is a rabbinic enactment with a practical goal: keeping the city's markets full. Knowing the reason explains why someone might think the rule should end once the בית המקדש was destroyed, which is what the next story is about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say'. The name of the speaker is reported in two versions.

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the rule has a practical reason connected to ירושלים, one could argue it lapses once that reason seems to disappear. רב יוסף's point is that it still stays in force until the Sages formally vote to cancel it.

phrases.english: And Ulla said,
and some say it was Rabba bar bar Chana,
phrases.notes: Two versions of who reported this statement.

phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
What is the reason for this rule?
In order to adorn the markets of Jerusalem with fruit.
phrases.notes: There would always be plenty of fruit in the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה טַעַם — כְּדֵי לְעַטֵּר שׁוּקֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם בְּפֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the enactment quoted in the ברייתא of Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The requirement to bring nearby fourth-year fruit to ירושלים was enacted so that the city's markets would be full of fruit.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's fourth-year vineyard near לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא about רבי אליעזר, who owned a fourth-year vineyard east of לוד, near כפר טבי. That location was inside the area that had to bring its fruit to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר had a fourth-year vineyard east of לוד, next to the village of כפר טבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story. It opens a new ברייתא and describes רבי אליעזר's vineyard, but the point of the story comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vineyard's location matters. East of לוד is toward ירושלים, so the vineyard fell inside the zone that was required to bring its fruit there. The story is building toward proof for רב יוסף: a rule made by a vote of the Sages stays in force until a new vote cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it was taught' in a ברייתא. This introduces a supporting source.
רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס, a student of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
A town west of ירושלים, at the edge of the day's-walk zone

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the proof. The ברייתא is only starting. The details about where the vineyard was are background for the event that comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer had a fourth-year vineyard
to the east of Lod, alongside the village of Tavi,
phrases.notes: That is, toward ירושלים, inside the zone that had to bring its fruit there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
